newsitem.title: FRANCE: French oil groups consider share buy-backs.
newsitem.headline: French oil groups consider share buy-backs.

text.p: French oil groups Elf-Aquitaine SA and Total SA on Thursday said separately of each other that they were seeking shareholder approval to buy back shares in the market.

But while Elf is planning to ask permission for a public buy-back offer (OPRA) -- stating a price at which it will buy -- Total plans to go to the market from time to time to buy depending on its share price.
Both companies aim to cancel the shares they would buy.

"It means that they believe there are not enough investment projects to put your money in that would yield a good enough return and that it's better to return money to shareholders," a French oil industry analyst said.

A spokeswoman for Elf said that the group would ask the May 30 shareholders' meeting for an authorisation to reduce its share capital by a total of 15 percent. The authorisation would be for a five-year period.
An Elf official said that the authorisation would give the company the option to buy back shares but it did not mean the company had already decided to do so.
At Total, a spokeswoman said that the company planned to ask permission on its May 21 general meeting to buy back up to 15 million shares, or 6.23 percent of its capital, for an 18 month period.
"Total is a growth stock and I believe they have plenty of opportunities to invest their cash instead of own shares," an industry analyst said.
Total will conduct the operation as a means to regularise its share price development, buying at a bottom level and if needed selling at a top level, and not as an OPRA.
According to analysts the method used by Total has more fiscal advantages than Elf's OPRA.
"I think Elf will need to ask finance ministry approval as well as shareholder approval," a Paris-based analyst said.

The result of a share buy-back and cancellation is that the net asset per share value and the earnings per share will increase. The dividend per share, if the total dividend pay-out out of profits is maintained, would also rise.
These factors would boost the share price.

The share markets welcomed the buyback news and Elf gained 1.26 percent to 562 francs while Total gained 1.85 percent to 473.90 francs while the Paris Bourse blue-chip index closed 0.22 percent lower.
While no major French company has executed an OPRA share buy-back, a number of them have been put in place in 1996 by Parfinance, Imaffine, Sceta, IDF and Zuberlaederich.
Four main listed companies have announced future OPRAs with Navigation Mixte -- controlled by Paribas -- aiming to buy back 40 percent of its capital at 875 francs per share.

Siparex wants to buy 12.5 percent of its capital at 135 francs per share and De Dietrich aims to acquire 18 percent of its capital at 275 francs. NSC will bid for 23 percent of its capital at 800 francs.
The idea is now catching on among blue-chips.
Schneider chairman Didier Pineau-Valencienne said on March 26 the electrical engineering company was considering buying back shares to boost earnings per share.
Seita chairman Jean-Dominique Commolli said a day later the tobacco group would seek authorisation to buy-back up to 15 percent of its capital for a five years. Seita's general meeting is on May 20.
